def update_zarr_node_digest(
    digest: "hashlib._Hash",
    node: "zarr.Group | zarr.Array",
    path: str,
) -> None:
    """Recursively fold a Zarr group/array's path, attrs, and data into ``digest``."""
    import zarr

    digest.update(path.encode("utf-8"))
    digest.update(b"\n")
    attrs_payload = {
        str(key): normalize_json_value(value) for key, value in sorted(node.attrs.items())
    }
    digest.update(canonical_json_bytes(attrs_payload))
    digest.update(b"\n")
    if isinstance(node, zarr.Array):
        update_array_digest(digest, np.asarray(node[...]))
        digest.update(b"\n")
        return
    for key in sorted(node.keys()):
        child = node[key]
        update_zarr_node_digest(digest, child, f"{path}/{key}")
items.why_relevant: Recursive digest: folds path, attrs, and array data into hash; processes root group and all nodes
Digest includes every node's attrs, sorted and JSON-canonicalized. No skip list or exclude mechanism.

suggestions: To root-cause test-rigor crash: run 'uv run python scripts/audit_test_rigor_gate.py --no-write-baseline 2>&1 | tee /tmp/test-rigor-crash.log' and capture stderr. If JSONDecodeError, check for the temp JSON report file and its contents. If file missing, pytest-cov did not generate it (check pytest exit code and stdout). If file exists but empty, pytest-cov generated the header but failed to write totals (check PYTEST_ADDOPTS override effectiveness).

For phase 2 pass-set pinning: consider a decision matrix: (a) if per-recipe metadata grows much larger (recipes needing multiple exempt reasons, time budgets, etc.), use a dedicated .praxia/audit_orphan_baseline.toml keyed by recipe name; (b) if mostly binary (passes/fails in CI), embed the baseline in audit_bootstrap_manifest.toml as a new [[orphans]] array; (c) if many recipes are CI-incapable, add a requires_ci() check in the script (similar to requires_arguments()) and split the output into runnable/needs_ci/needs_args three-way instead of two-way.

For per-recipe CI exemptions: establish pattern via Justfile comment + sys.exit(77) (pytest skip code) rather than skipping at workflow level. Allows test-gating to see the skip reason, aggregates exemptions visibly in one place (Justfile), and does not require bulk exemption list.
